stem.en: What does a scale of 1 cm = 500 m mean on a map?

text.en: 1 cm on the map stands for 500 m on the ground
500 cm on the map stand for 1 m on the ground

whyWrong.en: That would reverse the scale: the map is the smaller one, so a short map distance stands for a long ground distance.
The scale compares map length with ground length. It does not tell how wide the map is.

explanation.en: A scale compares a length on the map with the real distance on the ground.

stem.en: Which line is at 0 degrees latitude?

whyWrong.en: The Prime Meridian is 0 degrees longitude, a line from pole to pole.
That line is near 180 degrees longitude, opposite the Prime Meridian.

explanation.en: The Equator is the 0 degree parallel and divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

text.en: half circles running from one pole to the other
full circles parallel to the Equator

whyWrong.en: Those are parallels of latitude, which run east to west.

text.en: lines that measure distance from the poles

whyWrong.en: Longitude measures distance east or west of the Prime Meridian, not from the poles.

explanation.en: Meridians of longitude join the North Pole and the South Pole.

stem.en: The Earth is a perfect sphere.

explanation.en: It is nearly a sphere, slightly flattened at the poles.

stem.en: The Prime Meridian was fixed in 1884 to pass through

whyWrong.en: Ujjayini was the ancient Indian prime meridian, but the international one was fixed at Greenwich.
New York lies about 74 degrees West, far from 0 degrees.

explanation.en: Some nations agreed that the meridian through Greenwich would be the international Prime Meridian.

stem.en: By how many degrees does the Earth turn in one hour?

whyWrong.en: 24 is the number of hours in a day, not the degrees turned per hour.
30 degrees would take 12 hours for a full turn of 360, which is too fast.

explanation.en: 360 degrees divided by 24 hours is 15 degrees per hour.

stem.en: It is 12 noon in London. What is the time in India?

whyWrong.en: India is not at the Prime Meridian. Its standard time is ahead of GMT.
India is east of Greenwich, so its time is ahead, not behind.

explanation.en: Indian Standard Time is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.

stem.en: Crossing the International Date Line going east means you subtract a day.

explanation.en: Going east across the line you move from Monday to Sunday, and going west you add a day.

stem.en: Two places differ by 30 degrees of longitude. Their local times differ by

whyWrong.en: Each degree is 4 minutes of time, so 30 degrees is far more than 30 minutes.
1 hour would be only 15 degrees.

explanation.en: 30 divided by 15 degrees per hour is 2 hours.

text.en: A large place has no room to draw every building
Maps must always be in colour

whyWrong.en: Colour is not the reason. Symbols save space on any map.

text.en: Directions are not shown on maps

whyWrong.en: Directions are one of the three components of a map.

explanation.en: Symbols stand for features such as schools, roads and rivers so that many details fit on a small sheet.

stem.en: The ancient Indian prime meridian passed through

whyWrong.en: Greenwich is the modern international prime meridian, fixed in 1884.
Delhi is at about 77 degrees East and was not the prime meridian.

explanation.en: The madhya rekha, or middle line, passed through Ujjayini, a centre of astronomy.

stem.en: Why do some countries have more than one time zone?

text.en: They are very large from east to west
They want different times for fun

whyWrong.en: Time zones follow the Earth spin and country size, not choice for fun.

text.en: They are close to the Equator

whyWrong.en: Zones depend on east-west width, not on distance from the Equator.

explanation.en: The USA has six time zones and Russia has eleven because they stretch far from east to west.
